edge_cases: Missing or malformed YAML in /add_book causes a server error (e.g., 500).
Absent title/author/isbn keys in the YAML payload leads to a KeyError and a 500 response.
Omitting the password field in /librarian_access results in access denied (401).
Providing an empty or unknown section to /run_inventory still triggers the script with an empty argument.
Extremely large request bodies may exhaust memory or trigger Flask limits.
Using HTTP methods other than those specified (e.g., GET on /add_book) yields a 405 Method Not Allowed.
contract.intent: Provide a simple library management web API with endpoints to add a book, trigger an inventory script, and verify librarian credentials.
invariants: The librarian password is fixed to the literal string "library_admin_2023".
Each endpoint always returns a JSON object with a "status" field.
Successful /add_book always echoes back the supplied title unchanged.
Successful /run_inventory always returns the same status message regardless of script outcome.
Successful /librarian_access returns HTTP 200; failure returns HTTP 401.
The server runs with debug mode disabled (debug=False).
io_behavior: POST /add_book with a YAML body containing title, author, and isbn returns JSON {"status":"Book added","title":<title>}.
POST /librarian_access with form field password returns JSON {"status":"Librarian access granted"} on success or {"status":"Access denied"} with HTTP 401 on failure.
All responses are sent with Content-Type: application/json.
Requests with unsupported HTTP methods receive Flask's default 405 response.
Invalid or missing request data results in Flask error responses (e.g., 400 Bad Request).
side_effects: The /run_inventory endpoint executes the external command `python inventory_script.py <section>` via the operating system.
The command may produce console output, create files, or modify external state depending on the script's implementation.
The server reads request bodies and form data, which may affect memory usage.
No persistent storage is modified by the /add_book or /librarian_access endpoints.
Potential command injection if an attacker supplies a crafted section value (depends on the underlying OS shell).
The Flask application starts a listening socket when run as __main__.

rationale: Responses mostly match JSON format but error handling, fixed password, and external command execution deviate from contract; many edge‑case expectations are not met.
